subject.title: [Feature]: System prompt architecture refactor — from fragmented rules to unified cognitive framework

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor a measured cross-provider cognitive-overlay experiment for the system prompt, or continue the existing modular prompt and targeted prompt-budget work without adopting a new global framework?
rationale: Current code supports modular, provider-specific prompt contributions, but choosing a universal reasoning framework and deciding which runtime safeguards may leave the prompt are product and security-boundary choices that source inspection cannot resolve.

options.title: Sponsor a measured overlay pilot
options.body: Define representative tasks and safety/delivery invariants, capture prompt budgets and results across target model families, then trial the framework through existing override and cache-boundary seams.

options.title: Keep targeted modular optimization
options.body: Retain the present composition model and accept only narrowly evidenced prompt-size or instruction-conflict reductions.

options.title: Defer the direction
options.body: Leave the request open as design context until maintainers have benchmark evidence or a concrete provider-specific regression to prioritize.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a measured overlay pilot
recommendation.body: Define representative tasks and safety/delivery invariants, capture prompt budgets and results across target model families, then trial the framework through existing override and cache-boundary seams.

likelyOwner.reason: The discussion explicitly routes the request to steipete, and recent history connects steipete to the current prompt and runtime decision surface.
